newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom shares to go on sale May 20 - paper.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom shares to go on sale May 20 - paper.

text.p: A public offer of shares representing 20 percent of France Telecom is scheduled to begin on May 20, with stock trading expected to start at the beginning of June, the newspaper La Tribune said on Wednesday.

It said the public offer would run for a six-day period beginning on May 20. The government would have eight days from the close of the offer to determine the definitive price for the shares, the newspaper said, giving no indicative range for the offer price. It said the shares in state-controlled France Telecom would trade in Paris and possibly New York.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.

A three-week promotional campaign for the public offering, the biggest ever carried out in France, is expected to begin on the first weekend of May. The campaign is expected to announce a price range for the offering in its last week.

"But the definitive price will not be made public before the end of May," the newspaper said. "From the close of the offer, the government will have eight days to determine the price of the share. The finance ministry will base (its decision) on the breadth of demand and on the valuation of the company, which should be set at the end of May by the Privatisation Commission."
Brokerage BZW has valued France Telecom at 147 billion francs ($25.8 billion), but La Tribune said Merrill Lynch, which is advising France Telecom, has set a higher valuation.

It said the valuation was complicated by a multitude of exceptional items in the company's 1996 accounts, including a downward revision of its property holdings to 38 billion francs from 82 billion and a one-time transfer of 37.5 billion francs to the French state to cover pension liabilities.
The newspaper said the government was counting on the offer to increase the number of individual shareholders in France -- currently around 5.1 million.
"In sum, the sale of 20 percent of France Telecom, which would generate around 25 billion francs for the state, could touch...six million French people," the newspaper said.
The finance ministry will also study mechanisms to allow holders of bonds issued in 1993, maturing in July, to convert them into shares.

France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said earlier this month that the first France Telecom flotation would not be for less than $5 billion. The French state plans to retain a majority stake in France Telecom, but government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said last month that it would sell 20 percent.
